title: stage masks: matte threshold
shortDescription: Sonar: a calm survey of a deep-sea trench turns, ping by ping, into the same trench with something vast on its floor — matte() in 'threshold' mode, a living gray mask stage (a turning sweep, a boiling noise, pulse rings) swept by the progress
description:
A `StageDirector` with the stack `[trench, sonar display]`. The research sub hangs above a deep-sea trench, its floodlight pooling on the ooze: boulders, sea pens, glass sponges, marine snow drifting through the beam. The same view, the second time: a vast pale body lies along the floor, ringed and half buried, cyan parasites pulsing on its skin — and its eyes open, one after the other, along its whole length.

The change is `director.replace(survey, thing, {effect, duration, easing})` with `effect = matte({mask: ping, mode: 'threshold', softness})`. In **`'threshold'` mode** the gray of the mask stage is not the share of `to` but **when** a pixel switches: a pixel of coverage 0.3 switches at progress 0.3 — `lumaMask()` with a mask that lives. The mask stage `ping` is a `Stage2D` that is never in the stack and draws one opaque plane, read with `source: 'luminance'`; the director draws it only while the transition runs. Its TSL material is the sonar, animated by a clock of its own while the progress sweeps through it: *sonar sweep* — the angle behind a turning beam, so `to` shows in the wake of the sweep and the wake widens with the progress; *boiling noise* — a fractal noise that boils; *pulse rings* — the time since a ping front passed, near the sub first, then ring by ring (key K cycles them; the kind is a uniform, it changes mid-transition). Both ends hold by the switching function: at progress 0 every pixel shows the survey, at 1 every pixel the thing, whatever the sonar draws.

*matte softness* is how far a pixel blends around its switching point, in the range of the coverage. It is an option of `matte()`, so each value is an effect of its own — all six are made once and compiled ahead with `precompile()`. The *sonar display* is a layer above the slot, not part of the matte: it reads the same field from the same uniforms and the mask's `progressNode`, and draws the beam, the pings and, during a run, the front where the pixels switch, as wide as the softness. The **scope** in the corner shows the raw gray picture of the mask stage, the switched part tinted: the threshold idea at a glance. *scrub by hand* (key S) holds the progress on a slider (`manual: true`) — the sonar keeps moving, and the reveal moves with it. See [Stage masks: a transition through a living matte](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#a-transition-through-a-living-matte).
